title: Week 1 Sets NFL Scoring Record; Bears Post 59 Points, Bills Edge Texans Late, Ravens Dominate Colts
dek: NFL Week 1 Sunday, September 8, 2026, produced the most points scored on an opening Sunday since the 1970 merger. The Chicago Bears scored 59 points, their highest since 1980, in a 59-37 road win over Carolina. The Buffalo Bills defeated Houston 36-31 with the lead changing hands eight times. Baltimore defeated Indianapolis 41-23 behind strong performances from Zay Flowers and Derrick Henry.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: NFL Week 1 Sunday set a record for the most points scored on the opening Sunday of the season since the 1970 league merger, according to BBC Sport.
bottom_line: The Bills host their next playoff-caliber opponent in Week 2, while the Bears head into Week 2 still tracking toward Johnson's 37.9-points-per-game breakneck pace. The Ravens must absorb losses to Flowers and Lane before their next game. Watch whether Mayfield's behind-the-line pass rate proves sustainable for Tampa or signals scheme problems that mount; the Vikings' ninth starting quarterback in three years begins his second game against a playoff contender.
body:
NFL Week 1 Sunday, September 8, 2026, produced the most points scored on an opening Sunday of the season since the 1970 league merger, per BBC Sport. The showcase belonged chiefly to three teams: the Chicago Bears, who scored 59 points in a 59-37 road win over the Carolina Panthers; the Buffalo Bills, who defeated the Houston Texans 36-31 with the lead changing hands eight times; and the Baltimore Ravens, who routed the Indianapolis Colts 41-23.
The Bears' 59 points marked their highest output since 1980 and the highest-scoring Week One game in NFL history, according to ESPN. Chicago trailed Carolina 31-31 midway through the third quarter before outscoring the Panthers 28-6 the rest of the way. Quarterback Caleb Williams completed 21 of 29 passes for 269 yards and two passing touchdowns, and added two rushing touchdowns. ESPN reports Williams cleared 20 mph twice on those runs; since the start of last season, Williams has cleared that speed seven times as a ball carrier, more than the rest of the NFL's quarterbacks combined, who have six such plays total. His fastest touchdown was a 29-yard scamper at the end of the first half at 20.8 mph. Running back D'Andre Swift finished with three touchdowns.
The Bills' victory over Houston came down to precision timing. Allen passed for 334 yards and threw for two touchdowns while running in two more. ESPN reports the Bills had an explosive play rate of 21.2 percent, the highest ever achieved versus the Texans' defense under coach DeMeco Ryans. The Bills recorded nine completions of 16-plus yards and two runs of 12-plus yards, including a 21-yard scramble from Allen for an early touchdown. With less than two minutes remaining, Allen connected with Joshua Palmer on a 34-yard throw to clinch the win. Tight end Dalton Kincaid had 130 receiving yards, per ESPN, the most for a Bills tight end since 1967. Kincaid, who was recovering from a 2024 PCL injury to his left knee and played only 37 percent of snaps last season, played 76 percent of the offensive snaps in Week 1 with 40 total plays, his most in a game since Week 1 of last season.
Baltimore's dominant display featured two standout performances. Zay Flowers, the NFL's fourth highest-paid wide receiver, made five catches for a career-high 150 yards and a touchdown in the first half alone. Derrick Henry scored twice before halftime to move into third on the all-time list for rushing touchdowns, then added another in the Ravens' win. However, Flowers exited the second half with a hamstring injury, and rookie receiver Ja'Kobi Lane left the game with a wrist injury.
Injuries and scheme concerns surfaced elsewhere. The Minnesota Vikings defeated the Green Bay Packers 39-22 despite falling 22-10 down late in the third quarter. Kyler Murray, starting for the Vikings after being released by Arizona, had his first pass intercepted and suffered a concussion, forcing the team to rely on veteran Carson Wentz. Justin Jefferson claimed two touchdowns and a two-point conversion. The Vikings have cycled through nine starting quarterbacks since Jefferson won offensive player of the year in 2022. The Cincinnati Bengals defeated the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 33-27. The Bengals' revamped defense recorded four sacks and forced four fumbles, all recovered by Cincinnati, with one returned for a defensive touchdown. Baker Mayfield's pass attempts were 42.9 percent behind the line of scrimmage, per ESPN, a career high; the outlet notes this share is untenable in the modern NFL. The Arizona Cardinals upset the Los Angeles Chargers 26-14 at SoFi Stadium, which will host Super Bowl 61 in February.  The New York Giants defeated the Dallas Cowboys 28-20 in a primetime game at MetLife Stadium two days after the 25th anniversary of 9/11. Second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart passed for 230 yards and three touchdowns; running back Cam Skattebo rushed for a touchdown. The Giants honored first responders and those impacted by the attacks with a series of tributes.
Chicago's 59-point outburst aligns with head coach Ben Johnson's stated goal to break the 2013 Broncos' scoring record of 37.9 points per game. Johnson stated: "We want to be the highest scoring. We want to have the most wins. We want to win Super Bowls." The Bears' first-week output leaves them 21 points ahead of pace for the 2013 Broncos' season average over a 17-game schedule, assuming linear projection. ESPN notes 59 points is the fourth most in a game in the history of Chicago football. The Bills, meanwhile, face their first five games against teams viewed as potential Super Bowl contenders. The Chargers, despite being playoff contenders, were overmatched at home; defensive coordinator Chris O'Leary is stepping into the role vacated by Jesse Minter, now head coach of the Ravens after John Harbaugh's 18-year tenure ended. Minter's departure to Baltimore as head coach signals a defensive leadership change that the Chargers will need to prove they can absorb. The Texans, who owned the league's meanest defense last season, allowed 36 points and posted the worst explosive play rate allowed in Ryans' tenure since 2023.
Healthcare lingered in the shadows of offensive brilliance. The Buccaneers' scheme drew scrutiny after three of last season's 11 defeats came despite Tampa Bay scoring at least 34 points. The Vikings' quarterback instability persisted despite bringing in Murray: a concussion in Week 1 forced a quick pivot to Wentz. These vulnerabilities on the margins may reveal themselves more sharply as schedules deepen and injury lists grow.
